name: Wikidata (given names, surnames and colour names by language)
note: The answer to a question this campaign kept running into: there is no consolidated,
permissively licensed, pinnable dataset of names by language -- except that Wikidata is
one, if you query it rather than download it. The full dump is about 140 GB and 99.99%
of it is irrelevant; the queries in `fetch-wikidata-names.mjs` return exactly the names.
CC0. No attribution required, no share-alike, nothing to reconcile with Apache-2.0.
Decoy names it in NOTICE anyway, because being able to say where a value came from is
the point of the provenance machinery whether or not anyone requires it.
Marked `authored` for the same reason as Decoy's own lists: there is no artifact to
fetch and no integrity hash, because a SPARQL endpoint cannot be pinned -- it answers
with whatever Wikidata says today, it is rate-limited, and it returned a truncated body
mid-run while this was being set up. The query results are committed to the repository
instead, with the queries beside them, so the data can be re-derived and diffed. That
is checkable by inspection rather than only by comparison.
Colour names come from the same place and the same arrangement, queried by
`fetch-wikidata-colours.mjs`. One caution learned there applies to any future query: a
label tagged `fr` is not necessarily French. Where nobody has translated an item,
contributors paste the English string in and tag it anyway, which put `Fallow` and
`Flax` in a French colour list until the fetcher started comparing each label against
the item's English one.
Not weighted, and that matters: the US Census and INSEE lists carry how many people
bear each name, which is why `en` and `fr` produce realistic collision rates and these
locales do not. Wikidata records that a name exists, not how common it is. A national
registry replacing any of these lists is a straight upgrade.
